# crate

> Canonical schemas for data that changes shape, and provenance receipts
> for outputs.

crate declares a canonical shape for each file or table it registers. It
reads a registered file to that shape whichever known layout arrives, so
when upstream changes the file’s columns or layout, the fix is made once
in crate and code downstream keeps working; data read some other way is
held to the same shape. Its provenance receipt, one JSON file beside an
output, records how the output was made and what came out, so a rebuild
can be compared with its reference copy and judged identical, equivalent
within a declared tolerance, or different, naming what differed.

## Installation

``` r

pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/crate")
```

crate is under active development and its functions change between
releases (see
[NEWS](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/news/)). Pin a
release for reproducible work:
`pak::pak("NewGraphEnvironment/crate@vX.Y.Z")`.

## Example

[bcfishpass](https://github.com/smnorris/bcfishpass) reshaped
`user_habitat_classification.csv` from long to wide on 2026-04-26. crate
ships a small synthetic example of each shape, and one call reads either
to the same columns:

``` r

library(crate)

wide <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification",
  system.file("extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_wide.csv", package = "crate"))
long <- crt_ingest("bcfp", "user_habitat_classification",
  system.file("extdata/examples/bcfp/user_habitat_classification_long.csv", package = "crate"))
identical(names(wide), names(long))
#> [1] TRUE
```

One build was made twice from the same code, and its `km` column
differed in the 11th decimal place because the database summed in
another order. crate ships a synthetic copy of both builds with their
receipts:

``` r

wc <- system.file("extdata", "receipt", "examples", "worked_case", package = "crate")
crt_receipt_compare(file.path(wc, "build_1"), file.path(wc, "build_2"))
#> equivalent (receipts only; register v1.0.0)
#>   within result.parts[access_check.csv].bytes: 124 vs 128; table access_check agrees
#>   within result.parts[access_check.csv].sha256: "04994ff01cdee55d69fc410add51ad261ec4b33a751135fc224e97305823c3e2" vs "6801fb7bb092626441fd804d5ffbf8c4c05213ff18fa7c7ca524a9c2aa32f5e4"; table access_check agrees
#>   within result.summary[km_total]: 47.3767792597 vs 47.376779259805; within 1e-06
#>   record context.run: {"link_run_id":"20261104T181900Z-bulk"} vs {"link_run_id":"20261104T214400Z-bulk"}
#>   record context.time: "2026-11-04T18:22:05Z" vs "2026-11-04T21:47:31Z"
```

The file’s bytes differ, but the receipt says the file holds the
`access_check` table, whose fingerprint agrees under the declared `1e-9`
tolerance on `km`, and `km_total` differs within its `1e-6`, so the
builds are equivalent. The run identifiers and times are context,
recorded and never part of an identity.

## Learn more

- [How reading
  works](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/articles/reading.html):
  what crate knows about, one call reading two shapes of a file, and
  what happens between the file and the returned table.
- [Provenance
  receipts](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/articles/receipt.html):
  the receipt contract, writing a receipt and comparing two builds.
- Function reference:
  [Ingest](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/index.html#ingest),
  [Schemas](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/index.html#schemas)
  and [Provenance
  receipts](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/index.html#provenance-receipts).
- [Schemas](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/crate/blob/main/inst/extdata/schemas/README.md):
  the schema format, and how to register a new file or table.
- [STAC field
  schemas](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/crate/blob/main/pkgdown/assets/stac/README.md):
  JSON Schemas for custom fields a STAC item can list in
  `stac_extensions`, published with crate’s website.

## Ecosystem

| Package | Role |
|----|----|
| **crate** | Canonical schemas for data that changes shape, and provenance receipts for outputs (this package) |
| [fresh](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/fresh/) | Stream network modelling engine: segment, classify, cluster, aggregate |
| [link](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/link/) | Intrinsic habitat models: develop, test and communicate |
| [wet](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/wet/) | Stream flow and water temperature for BC’s Freshwater Atlas |
| [flooded](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/flooded/) | Delineate floodplain extents from DEMs and stream networks |
| [drift](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/drift/) | Track land cover change within floodplains over time |
| [floodplains](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/floodplains/) | Floodplain and land cover change modelling for BC watershed groups |
| [stac_floodplains_bc](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/stac_floodplains_bc/) | STAC catalogue of floodplain land cover change in BC, 2017-2023, by watershed group |
| [cd](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/cd/) | Climate departure analysis from ERA5-Land reanalysis |
| [fly](https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/fly/) | Estimate airphoto footprints and select photos that cover a study area |

``` r
citation("crate")
```

# Package index

## Ingest

Read a registered source file to its canonical shape.

- [`crt_ingest()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_ingest.md)
  : Ingest a registered upstream file and return canonical-shape data
- [`crt_files()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_files.md)
  : List registered (source, file_name) entries crate knows how to
  ingest

## Schemas

Declared canonical shapes, and conforming a frame to one.

- [`crt_schema_cols()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_schema_cols.md)
  : What each column of a registered schema means
- [`crt_schema_conform()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_schema_conform.md)
  : Conform a data frame to a registered canonical schema
- [`crt_schema_fingerprint()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_schema_fingerprint.md)
  : Fingerprint a capture's column set
- [`crt_schema_grade()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_schema_grade.md)
  : Which records can answer which question
- [`crt_schema_variant()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_schema_variant.md)
  : Name the known version each record was captured with

## Provenance receipts

Write, read and compare one receipt per output: how it was made and what
came out, judged identical, equivalent within a declared tolerance, or
different.

- [`crt_receipt_compare()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_compare.md)
  : Compare two provenance receipts
- [`crt_receipt_keys()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_keys.md)
  : Read a package's receipt declaration
- [`crt_receipt_migrate()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_migrate.md)
  : Read an older provenance record as a receipt
- [`crt_receipt_read()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_read.md)
  : Read a provenance receipt
- [`crt_receipt_stac()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_stac.md)
  : A receipt's fields as a STAC item mirrors them
- [`crt_receipt_validate()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_validate.md)
  : Validate a provenance receipt
- [`crt_receipt_write()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_receipt_write.md)
  : Write a provenance receipt
- [`crt_table_fingerprint()`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/crate/reference/crt_table_fingerprint.md)
  : Fingerprint a table's values
